key_insight: HASA uses each pretrained attention head’s query-key interaction structure to adapt sparse selection across both feature directions and context regions.
engineering_relevance: This training-free approach targets long-context inference costs by selecting relevant regions cheaply before computing exact attention with their original full-dimensional KV states.
method: Derive a head-specific compact response space from the query-key operator’s singular spectrum.
Progressively merge neighboring context regions with directionally coherent responses, keeping heterogeneous regions separate.
Select regions in the compact space, then compute exact attention using their full-dimensional KV states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 88.1% dense-attention mass capture, accuracy gains over UNIQUE of up to 3.47 points on RULER and 2.57 on LongBench-Pro, and self-attention speedups up to 1.32× over UNIQUE and 14.07× over dense attention.
watch_item: Reported speedups concern self-attention rather than end-to-end inference; practical gains should be checked against selection overhead and deployment hardware.
paper_title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure
